title: 220. Algebra, Equations & Inequalities: Inequalities Involving Exponential Functions
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Solving exponential inequalities with base greater than \(1\)
questions.question: Solve \(2^x>8\).
questions.explanation: Write \(8\) as a power of \(2\): \(8=2^3\). The inequality becomes \(2^x>2^3\). Since the base \(2\) is greater than \(1\), the exponential function is increasing, so the inequality preserves direction. Therefore \(x>3\).
questions.hint: Rewrite both sides with the same base, then compare the exponents.

questions.concept: Solving exponential inequalities with base greater than \(1\)
questions.learningObjective: Solve \(a^{x+b}\le a^c\) for \(a>1\) by comparing exponents.
questions.question: Solve \(3^{x-1}\le27\).
questions.explanation: Write \(27\) as a power of \(3\): \(27=3^3\). The inequality becomes \(3^{x-1}\le3^3\). Since the base \(3\) is greater than \(1\), the exponential function is increasing, so \(x-1\le3\). Therefore \(x\le4\).
questions.hint: Express \(27\) as a power of \(3\), then compare the exponents.

questions.concept: Solving exponential inequalities with base between \(0\) and \(1\)
questions.learningObjective: Solve \(a^x>a^c\) for \(0<a<1\) by reversing the inequality when comparing exponents.
questions.question: Solve \(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^x>4\).
questions.explanation: Write \(4\) as a power of \(\frac{1}{2}\): \(4=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{-2}\). The inequality becomes \(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^x>\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{-2}\). Since the base \(\frac{1}{2}\) is between \(0\) and \(1\), the exponential function is decreasing, so the inequality direction reverses: \(x<-2\).
questions.hint: Rewrite \(4\) as a power of \(\frac{1}{2}\), and remember that a base between \(0\) and \(1\) reverses the inequality.

questions.concept: Solving exponential inequalities with a linear exponent
questions.learningObjective: Solve an exponential inequality by converting to equal bases and comparing exponents.
questions.question: Solve \(5^{2x-1}\ge125\).
questions.explanation: Write \(125\) as a power of \(5\): \(125=5^3\). The inequality becomes \(5^{2x-1}\ge5^3\). Since the base \(5\) is greater than \(1\), \(2x-1\ge3\). Therefore \(2x\ge4\), so \(x\ge2\).
questions.hint: Rewrite \(125\) as \(5^3\), then solve the resulting linear inequality.

questions.concept: Solving exponential inequalities with base between \(0\) and \(1\)
questions.learningObjective: Solve an exponential inequality by rewriting with a base between \(0\) and \(1\) and reversing the inequality.
questions.question: Solve \(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{x+1}<8\).
questions.explanation: Write \(8\) as a power of \(\frac{1}{2}\): \(8=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{-3}\). The inequality becomes \(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{x+1}<\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{-3}\). Since the base \(\frac{1}{2}\) is between \(0\) and \(1\), the exponential function is decreasing, so \(x+1>-3\). Therefore \(x>-4\).
questions.hint: Rewrite \(8\) as a power of \(\frac{1}{2}\), then reverse the inequality when comparing exponents.

questions.concept: Solving exponential inequalities by converting to a common base
questions.learningObjective: Solve an inequality involving powers with different bases by converting both sides to base \(2\).
questions.question: Solve \(4^x\le8^{x-1}\).
questions.explanation: Write both sides with base \(2\): \(4^x=(2^2)^x=2^{2x}\), and \(8^{x-1}=(2^3)^{x-1}=2^{3x-3}\). The inequality becomes \(2^{2x}\le2^{3x-3}\). Since the base \(2\) is greater than \(1\), \(2x\le3x-3\). Therefore \(x\ge3\).
questions.hint: Convert \(4\) and \(8\) to powers of \(2\), then compare the exponents.

questions.concept: Solving exponential inequalities by converting to a common base
questions.learningObjective: Solve an inequality involving powers with different bases by converting both sides to base \(3\).
questions.question: Solve \(9^x>27^{x-1}\).
questions.explanation: Write both sides with base \(3\): \(9^x=(3^2)^x=3^{2x}\), and \(27^{x-1}=(3^3)^{x-1}=3^{3x-3}\). The inequality becomes \(3^{2x}>3^{3x-3}\). Since the base \(3\) is greater than \(1\), \(2x>3x-3\). Therefore \(x<3\).
questions.hint: Convert \(9\) and \(27\) to powers of \(3\), then solve the resulting linear inequality.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a natural exponential inequality by comparing exponents.
questions.question: Solve \(e^{x+2}>e^{3x}\).
questions.explanation: The base \(e\) is greater than \(1\), so the exponential function \(e^u\) is increasing. Therefore \(e^{x+2}>e^{3x}\) implies \(x+2>3x\). Solving gives \(2>2x\), so \(x<1\).
questions.hint: Since \(e>1\), the inequality direction is preserved when comparing the exponents.

questions.concept: Solving exponential inequalities with base between \(0\) and \(1\)
questions.learningObjective: Solve an exponential inequality by rewriting with base \(\frac{1}{3}\) and reversing the inequality.
questions.question: Solve \(\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{x-2}\ge\frac{1}{9}\).
questions.explanation: Write \(\frac{1}{9}\) as a power of \(\frac{1}{3}\): \(\frac{1}{9}=\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^2\). The inequality becomes \(\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{x-2}\ge\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^2\). Since the base \(\frac{1}{3}\) is between \(0\) and \(1\), the exponential function is decreasing, so \(x-2\le2\). Therefore \(x\le4\).
questions.hint: Rewrite \(\frac{1}{9}\) as \(\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^2\), then reverse the inequality when comparing exponents.

questions.concept: Solving exponential inequalities with a quadratic exponent
questions.learningObjective: Solve an exponential inequality by comparing exponents and solving the resulting quadratic inequality.
questions.question: Solve \(2^{x^2}>2^{3x-2}\).
questions.explanation: Since the base \(2\) is greater than \(1\), the inequality \(2^{x^2}>2^{3x-2}\) implies \(x^2>3x-2\). Rearranging gives \(x^2-3x+2>0\). Factor: \((x-1)(x-2)>0\). The product is positive when \(x<1\) or \(x>2\). Therefore the solution is \(x<1\) or \(x>2\).
questions.hint: Compare the exponents, then solve the resulting quadratic inequality.
